questions.question: Origin and development of Syriac language.
questions.solution_html:
• Syriac originated as a dialect of Aramaic in Edessa .around the 1st century AD. It
  • evolved into a distinct language by the 3rd century, becoming a major literary and liturgical
  • language of the Syriac Christians. Syriac flourished from the 3rd to the 7th centuries
  • producing significant theological, philosophical, and literary works.

questions.question: What moral message does Ahikar’s story convey?
questions.solution_html:
• Wisdom of Ahiqar
  • The story of the Aramean sage Ahiqar is perhaps the most widely circulated piece of Aramaic
  • literature- He had no sons- He adopted sister’s son- Nadan plotted against his uncle- Ahiqar
  • was sentenced to death and handed over to the executioner- But executionaer saved his life
  • and revealed the truth to the king- So Nadan was punished
questions.final_answer: and revealed the truth to the king- So Nadan was punished

questions.question: How does the story of ten lepers reflects Jesus’ compassion and power?
questions.solution_html:
• The story of the 10 lepers (Luke 17:11-19) showcases Jesus' compassion and power.
  • Compassion; Jesus shows mercy to the marginalized lepers, healing them despite their social
  • exclusion.
  • He responds to their plea for mercy, demonstrating God's love for the suffering.
  • Power; Jesus heals all 10 lepers with a single command, "Go show yourselves to the priests."
  • The healing is instant, highlighting Jesus' divine authority over disease and suffering.
  • Only one leper returns to thank Jesus, highlighting the importance of gratitude and faith.
questions.final_answer: Only one leper returns to thank Jesus, highlighting the importance of gratitude and faith

questions.question: Describe the events leading up to the battle between David and Goliath?
questions.solution_html:
• Story of David and Goliath
  • The Philistines gathered their armies to fight Israel, and a giant warrior named Goliath
  • challenged the Israelites to a one-on-one battle. For 40 days, Goliath taunted the Israelites
  • but no one dared to fight him. David, a young shepherd, arrived at the battlefield with food
  • for his brothers and accepted the challenge. Armed with a sling and stones, David faced
  • Goliath, trusting in God's power

questions.question: How does the story of ten lepers reflects Jesus’ compassion and power?
questions.solution_html:
• The story of the 10 lepers (Luke 17:11-19) showcases Jesus' compassion and power.
  • Compassion; Jesus shows mercy to the marginalized lepers, healing them despite their social
  • exclusion.
  • He responds to their plea for mercy, demonstrating God's love for the suffering.
  • Power; Jesus heals all 10 lepers with a single command, "Go show yourselves to the priests."
  • The healing is instant, highlighting Jesus' divine authority over disease and suffering.
  • Only one leper returns to thank Jesus, highlighting the importance of gratitude and faith.
questions.final_answer: Only one leper returns to thank Jesus, highlighting the importance of gratitude and faith
